newsitem.title: UK: UK UNEMPLOYMENT FALLS 49,800 IN JULY.
newsitem.headline: UK UNEMPLOYMENT FALLS 49,800 IN JULY.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics released the following provisional data for unemployment in July and average earnings in June. (Previous estimates in brackets, minus denotes fall, data seasonally adjusted unless indicated)
NOTE - Mkts forecast 31,000 July unemployment fall
NOTE: Consensus forecast 4.25 pct for overall underlying average earnings.
UNIT WAGE COSTS JUNE MAY (PREL MAY)
EMPLOYEES IN EMPLOYMENT Q1 Q4 Q1 1996
JOB CENTRE VACANCIES JULY JUNE (PREL JUN)
* Adjusted unemployment rate the lowest since April 1990
The ONS said this was the 17th consecutive monthly fall in unemployment.
It said long-term unemployment stood at 531,000 in July, down 248,000 on the same period last year.
Each July, inflows to the claimant count are large because of an influx of school and college leavers. But this year, the influx was smaller than in previous years.
Unemployment among 18-24-year olds comprised 26.7 percent of the overall total. There are now 440,000 unemployed who could be affected by the new deal scheme.
The number of employees in manufacturing rose by 3,000 in June to stand at 3,944,000, up 25,000 in the year to June.
It has just been discovered that vacancy statistics have been exaggerated due to collection problems which are being addressed.
The total number of vacancies has therefore been exaggerated by about 40,000.
According to the Labour Force Survey, unemployment is falling at between 20,000 to 35,000 each month.
